title: Difference Quotient of a Linear Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For f(x)=3x+1, evaluate the difference quotient (f(x+h)-f(x))/h, h != 0, and interpret the constant result.

steps.title: Compute f(x+h)
steps.explanation: Distribute the 3 across the incremented input.
steps.why: Linearity means the increment simply adds 3h.

steps.title: Subtract f(x)
steps.explanation: Both the 3x and the +1 cancel, leaving only 3h.
steps.why: For a linear rule, the change is proportional to the increment.

steps.title: Divide by h
steps.explanation: Canceling h yields the constant 3, independent of x and h.
steps.why: The difference quotient of a linear function is its slope, here 3.
